domain: Geographic page system — subdivisions, neighborhoods, master-planned communities, cities
summary: The prior audit was directionally right on architecture but wrong on three material findings, all from not searching hard enough. (1) A searchable A-to-Z index of EVERY community/subdivision with active inventory does exist and ships — components/community/CommunityIndexBrowser.tsx rendered at app/communities/page.tsx:428 — the auditor called it "missing". (2) School attendance-zone GIS polygons DO exist (geo_type='school', Deschutes County GIS, migration 20260704120000) and are rendered on /schools/[slug]; the auditor declared them nonexistent based on a component docstring. (3) The long-tail subdivision content tier is /communities/{city}-{sub}, which renders the FULL ~18-section stack, not the deliberately-thin /subdivisions/[slug] plat route the auditor benchmarked. What survives and is worse than stated: the sitemap emits /cities/{city}/{sub} for every (city, subdivision) pair while the correct working route /communities/{city}-{sub} exists and is never emitted — and the middleware hard-404 guard only matches single-segment /cities paths, so those URLs likely land as hollow soft-404s, the exact failure mode the middleware was written to kill. Events/parks/regulations remain absent as geo-scoped content. Out-of-area MLS coverage remains architecturally excluded.

items.requirement: No difference between a plain community/city landing page and a master-planned community page
items.evidence: Confirmed by reading all four page files. KbSchools imported only at app/communities/[slug]/page.tsx:94 and rendered at :902 — no KbSchools import in app/cities/[slug]/page.tsx or app/cities/[slug]/[neighborhoodSlug]/page.tsx (grep across all four returned nothing). KbCommunityAlerts only at communities/[slug]/page.tsx:93,936. STR/second-home block at communities/[slug]/page.tsx:942-951. KbResortOverview appears on BOTH communities/[slug]/page.tsx:864 AND cities/[slug]/[neighborhoodSlug]/page.tsx:495 (auditor said community-only — wrong for the neighborhood tier). City-unique blocks confirmed: neighborhoods ledger cities/[slug]/page.tsx:607-613, golf/master-planned ledger :637-645, lifestyle links :619-631. All four share KbAbout/KbMarketHud/FAQBlock except subdivisions/[slug].
items.gap: [CORRECTED: KbResortOverview is NOT community-only — it renders on the city-neighborhood page too (cities/[slug]/[neighborhoodSlug]/page.tsx:495), so the divergence is narrower than claimed.] Real remaining divergence: KbSchools + KbCommunityAlerts + the STR note render only on /communities/[slug]; the neighborhoods and golf ledgers render only on /cities/[slug]. Four page types each hand-pick their section list with no shared archetype, so drift is structural, not accidental.
items.why_it_matters: Matt's explicit instruction. Four independent hand-maintained section stacks means every new section has to be added four times or it silently diverges again.

items.requirement: Every geo page covers community events, new rules/regulations, potential city impacts, and parks
items.evidence: Re-ran the search. data/co-events.ts, co-parks.ts, co-trails.ts, co-venues.ts are consumed ONLY by app/central-oregon/{events,venues,trails}/*, app/parks/*, app/sitemap.ts, lib/data/{events,parks,venues,trails}/*, and components/site/listing-detail/ParksNearbyBlock.tsx — grep -rln across app/cities, app/communities, app/subdivisions returns zero. BUT the auditor missed that every geo page renders KbNav + KbFooter, which DO link these silos site-wide: components/site/kb/KbNav.client.tsx:50-61 (/schools, /parks, /central-oregon/events, /venues, /trails, /lp/central-oregon-golf) and KbFooter.client.tsx:122-125. Regulations/city-impacts: confirmed zero — no zoning/ordinance/annexation/city-council module anywhere in lib/, data/, or components/site/kb/.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: not "missing" — global nav and footer on every geo page link events, parks, trails, venues, golf, and schools. What is missing is GEO-SCOPED surfacing: no "parks in Sisters", no "events near Tetherow", no per-city regulatory feed.] Regulations / new rules / city impacts are genuinely absent with no data source, no component, and no route.
items.why_it_matters: A site-wide nav link is not per-geo content and earns no topical relevance for "<neighborhood> parks" or "<city> short-term rental rules" queries. The registries already carry city fields, so geo-scoping them is a join, not a data-collection project.

items.requirement: Master-plan community pages additionally cover the neighborhoods within them (neighborhoods contain subdivisions, hierarchy both ways)
items.evidence: Verified both directions. Downward (neighborhood → subdivisions) is built: cities/[slug]/[neighborhoodSlug]/page.tsx uses getCommunitiesInNeighborhood (imported line 27). Upward is cut by an explicit code comment at communities/[slug]/page.tsx:539 ("Sub-neighborhood ledger intentionally omitted: the registry has no per-sub active count or median"). Root cause corroborated from source, not docs: migration 20260515170000_resort_communities_neighborhood_aliases.sql adds the 14 resort communities as geo_type='neighborhood' rows in `boundaries` with 100 name aliases in `neighborhood_subdivisions` — there is no sub-neighborhood tier BELOW a resort community in that model at all.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] The community page renders KbCommunities (communities/[slug]/page.tsx:878) — a city-scoped rail — instead of a contained-neighborhoods ledger. The data model has no sub-neighborhood tier under a resort community, so this is a schema gap, not a UI omission. The code's own comment admits it.
items.why_it_matters: Named explicitly by Matt. Fixing it requires either per-alias market rows or a name+link-only ledger — a §0 decision, not an engineering one.

items.requirement: A searchable site index covering thousands of subdivisions, dozens of neighborhoods, and master-plan communities
items.evidence: THE AUDITOR WAS WRONG. app/communities/page.tsx:170 builds `indexItems` from getCommunitiesForIndex() — which (app/actions/communities.ts:58-140) aggregates EVERY (city, SubdivisionName) pair across all active listing tiles, not the curated 19 — and renders it at line 428 via <CommunityIndexBrowser items={indexItems} />. components/community/CommunityIndexBrowser.tsx:1 is a client component with a search Input (line 114) filtering by community or city name (line 95), each row linking to /communities/{slug} (line 44). Page copy at app/communities/page.tsx:422-424 states the count and "Search by name or city, or browse the index." These long-tail city-prefixed slugs are NOT blocked by middleware — isInvalidGeoSlug (middleware.ts:270-274) admits any slug passing isCentralOregonCommunitySlug().
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor called this "missing" after only running `ls app/subdivisions/`. A working, shipping, client-side-searchable A-to-Z index of every community/subdivision with active inventory exists at /communities.] Real remaining gaps: the index covers only subdivisions with CURRENT active listings (not the 3,213 plat rows in `boundaries`), there is no index for the plat-level /subdivisions/[slug] route, and no index of the 13 Bend neighborhoods.
items.why_it_matters: Downgrading this from missing to partial changes the scope from "build an index" to "widen the existing index's source query".

items.requirement: Every page 100% optimized for search indexing, no thin content
items.evidence: app/subdivisions/[slug]/page.tsx is 446 lines and renders only KbHero, optional VideoTourRail, optional KbListingMap, KbFeatured, KbSell, KbFooter — confirmed by import list (lines 41-53), no KbAbout/KbMarketHud/KbSchools/KbArticles/FAQBlock. BUT the auditor benchmarked the wrong tier. That route's own docstring (lines 3-9) states it is the PLAT-level boundary route linked from KbResortOverview chips, deliberately stripped of market sections "too thin to be honest at plat level (CLAUDE.md §0)". The real subdivision content tier is /communities/{city}-{sub}, served by the 975-line communities/[slug]/page.tsx, which renders the full stack (KbMarketHud :856, KbResortOverview :864, KbAbout :871, KbCommunities :878, KbAreaGuideVideo, KbOpenHouses, KbActivity, KbSchools :902, KbArticles, KbExploreTowns, FAQBlock :968) for long-tail non-resort slugs too, not just the 19 resorts.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor claimed subdivisions are "the tier meant to cover thousands of geos" and are therefore textbook thin content. They are not that tier — /communities/{city}-{sub} is, and it is full-featured.] What survives: /subdivisions/[slug] IS thin (6 sections) and is crawlable via KbResortOverview chips, so thin pages are reachable and indexable with no noindex. Its thinness is a deliberate §0 tradeoff documented in code, not an oversight.

items.requirement: Every geo page pre-built / discoverable (generateStaticParams + crawlability)
items.evidence: Confirmed literally. app/subdivisions/[slug]/page.tsx:58-59 `return []`. app/cities/[slug]/[neighborhoodSlug]/page.tsx:81-83 `return []`. Both are listed as tracked violators in scripts/static-params-baseline.json lines 8 and 22. cities/[slug]/page.tsx:92 returns PRIMARY_CITIES.map(...). communities/[slug]/page.tsx:114 returns getAllResortCommunities().map(...) — 19 resorts only; the ~1,800 long-tail community slugs also get zero SSG. All four set dynamicParams=true, revalidate=60.
items.gap: [VERIFIED, and broader than stated] The auditor named neighborhoods and subdivisions. The long-tail /communities/{city}-{sub} pages — the actual subdivision content tier — also get zero build-time SSG (only the 19 registry slugs are seeded), so the largest page family in the system cold-renders on demand.

items.requirement: Sitemap correctness for the geo tree (a prerequisite for '100% optimized for search indexing')
items.evidence: Read app/sitemap.ts:312-339 in full. subsByCity is built from every (City, SubdivisionName) active pair filtered to cityNameSet (line 325), then line 335 emits `/cities/{cityKey}/{subSlug}`. That route resolves via getNeighborhoodBySlug → getNeighborhoodBySlugInCity (app/actions/cities.ts:415-425), an exact (city_id, slug) lookup against `neighborhoods` with NO subdivision fallback — null → notFound() in generateMetadata (cities/[slug]/[neighborhoodSlug]/page.tsx). `neighborhoods` being Bend-districts-only is corroborated from SOURCE, not just docs: lib/subdivision-area-redirects.ts:34-36 documents "The 13 City-of-Bend GIS neighborhoods, served by the city-neighborhood route," built from data/bend/bend-neighborhood-polygons.json tier:'city'. Worse than the auditor found: middleware's hard-404 guard isInvalidGeoSlug (middleware.ts:262-276) matches ONLY `^/cities/([^/]+)/?$` — single segment — so two-segment /cities/{city}/{sub} misses the guard entirely and falls into the exact hollow-200 soft-404 path the guard's own comment (middleware.ts:244-252) says Google files under 'crawled, not indexed'. Separately confirmed: `/subdivisions/` appears nowhere in app/sitemap.ts, and /communities emission (line 303) is limited to RESORT_COMMUNITY_SLUGS, so the ~1,800 long-tail community pages that DO render correctly are also absent.
items.gap: [VERIFIED and escalated] Not just 404s — likely soft-404 hollow 200s, the worst outcome, because the middleware guard does not cover two-segment /cities paths. And the fix is trivial in a way the auditor missed: /communities/{city}-{sub} already renders full content for exactly these pairs and is already whitelisted by middleware, so the sitemap is emitting a broken URL pattern while the working one sits unused. Three defects in one function: wrong route emitted, correct route omitted, /subdivisions omitted entirely.
items.why_it_matters: This is a currently-shipping regression that actively suppresses indexing. One line change at app/sitemap.ts:335 redirects the whole volume at a route that already works.

items.requirement: Cover ALL subdivisions in the MLS, including cities outside the primary Central Oregon service area (e.g. Burns), for referral-fee lead capture
items.evidence: Read lib/central-oregon.ts in full (59 lines). CENTRAL_OREGON_CITY_SLUGS is a hardcoded 25-slug tri-county set (lines 13-22, not ~22). The header comment (lines 1-10) states the explicit purpose: keep out-of-area cities out of the communities index, sitemap, and geo links. Enforced at app/sitemap.ts:276 (isCentralOregonCity), app/actions/communities.ts index path, and middleware.ts:262-276, which serves a hard 404 with a body reading "That place is not in our Central Oregon coverage" (GEO_NOT_FOUND_HTML, middleware.ts:279-284). grep -rniE 'burns|harney' across app/ lib/ data/ components/ returns only Ken Burns CSS animations and unrelated prose. No referral-capture route, no out-of-area lead rule.
items.gap: [VERIFIED — and stronger than stated] The exclusion is not passive. middleware.ts ships a hand-written 404 page whose copy explicitly tells an out-of-area visitor the place is outside coverage, then sends them to /homes-for-sale. That is an active rejection of the referral lead Matt asked to capture.
items.why_it_matters: Direct named business requirement. The 404 body is a lead-capture surface today serving a dead end — the cheapest possible first increment is replacing that copy with a capture form.

items.requirement: Boundaries come from official GIS (city/county) polygons for neighborhoods, subdivisions, parks, school districts, trails
items.evidence: THE AUDITOR WAS WRONG ON SCHOOLS AND WRONG TO DOUBT PARKS. Migration supabase/migrations/20260704120000_boundaries_allow_school_type.sql widens boundaries_geo_type_check to include 'park' AND 'school', and adds upsert_boundary() (revoked from anon+authenticated). scripts/seo-import-school-boundaries.mjs imports Deschutes County GIS "School Attendance Area" polygons (maps.deschutes.org BoundaryFD MapServer layer 19, outSR=4326) covering Bend-La Pine 601, Redmond 620, Sisters 640, with explicit refuse-to-guess matching. app/schools/[slug]/page.tsx:114-129 renders that polygon via getGeoBoundaryMapData({geoType:'school'}) and labels it "<school> attendance area". Parks: migration 20260603130000_park_boundaries.sql exists; lib/data/parks/getParkBoundaryGeoJSON.ts reads geo_type='park'; app/parks/[slug]/page.tsx:119 gates on park.hasPolygon. Trails confirmed absent: grep -cniE 'coordinates|geometry|polygon|"path"' data/co-trails.ts returns 0.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor asserted "School district GIS boundaries don't exist" from a KbSchools.tsx docstring, and speculated park polygons might not exist because a doc's 3,251 breakdown left "no headroom". Both wrong — the doc is simply stale (parks and schools were added in later migrations). The auditor trusted a component comment and a .md over two migrations and a working route.] Real gaps: trails have no geometry at all; school attendance polygons cover only three Deschutes districts (Crook/Jefferson unimported); and school attendance zones are NOT surfaced on any geo page — KbSchools still renders a district-name text mapping only, even though the polygons now exist one DAL call away.
items.why_it_matters: The polygons Matt asked for mostly exist and are authoritative. The failure is distribution, not sourcing — geo pages don't consume data the site already owns.

shared_primitives_needed: A single geo-page ARCHETYPE (one shared section-stack component parameterized by tier) replacing the four hand-maintained import lists in app/cities/[slug], app/cities/[slug]/[neighborhoodSlug], app/communities/[slug], app/subdivisions/[slug] — today adding a section means editing four files or accepting drift

A sitemap URL resolver that emits only routes proven to resolve, plus extension of middleware's isInvalidGeoSlug regex to multi-segment /cities/{city}/{sub} paths so unresolvable geo URLs return a hard 404 instead of a hollow 200

A geo-scoped local-context join (events, parks, trails, venues, schools-with-attendance-polygons already exist as data; regulations/city-impacts do not) surfacing 'near this place' rather than site-wide nav links
Per-sub-neighborhood market-stats rows, or an explicit name-and-link-only ledger contract, so /communities/[slug] can list contained neighborhoods without violating §0

A canonical hierarchy registry reconciling data/resort-communities.json (19), the communities aggregation in getCommunitiesForIndex (live-listing-derived), `neighborhoods` (13 Bend districts), `neighborhood_subdivisions` (aliases), and `boundaries` geo_type∈{city,neighborhood,subdivision,park,school}
open_questions_for_owner: The /communities A-to-Z index only lists subdivisions with CURRENT active listings. Should it also enumerate the ~3,213 plat-level subdivisions from `boundaries` that have zero active inventory, or does a page with no listings fail your bar?

For out-of-area MLS cities like Burns: the site currently serves a hand-written 404 saying 'That place is not in our Central Oregon coverage.' Do you want that replaced with a referral capture form, full branded geo pages, or left as-is?

School attendance-area polygons already exist for Bend-La Pine, Redmond, and Sisters but are only drawn on /schools/[slug]. Do you want them on city/neighborhood/community pages too, and should Crook/Jefferson district polygons be imported to close the coverage gap?

'New rules/regulations' and 'potential city impacts' have no data source anywhere in the repo. Is there a feed (city council agendas, county planning RSS) you want ingested, or is this an editorial workflow?
Should the community→neighborhood ledger ship name-and-link-only now, or wait for per-sub-neighborhood market data so every number stays verified per §0?
